20261125.background: 黄仁勋在这组连续报道中因婚外情、国家安全疑云和公司治理争议一度离开英伟达，随后又在股东、硅谷领袖和特朗普的施压下迅速复职。文章借此讨论一个更大的问题：当人工智能热潮、美国股市和经济信心都高度依赖英伟达及其创始人时，正常的监管、问责和董事会独立性是否会被经济利益架空。
20261125.overview:
文章用“英伟达国家”和“人质经济”两个比喻批评黄仁勋复职。黄仁勋离开仅11天便重返英伟达，科技股随即强势反弹，英伟达股价上涨31%。支持者认为他是AI繁荣与美国科技领导力不可替代的核心，没有他，投资者信心和AI泡沫都可能崩塌。

作者认为，这种说法掩盖了真正的利益：政府、投资者和科技公司需要维持由循环融资、巨额债务和持续采购芯片支撑的AI热潮，同时借黄仁勋回归树立“推动AI的人可以凌驾于规则之上”的先例。民调与国会议员的质疑并未改变结果。文章最终警告，当经济安全、国家安全和退休储蓄被用作交换服从的筹码时，社会面对的已不只是公司人事问题，而是一场以经济崩盘相威胁的“人质危机”。
20261125.pet:
The article says that Americans now live in an “Nvidiastate”. This is not a real country. It is a way of saying that Nvidia and its CEO have become too important to the economy. People seem to have only two choices: allow AI leaders to act without limits, or risk a recession.

Jensen Huang returned to Nvidia only eleven days after leaving the company. Shareholders, Silicon Valley leaders and President Trump had all pushed for his return. The stock market reacted strongly. Nvidia shares rose 31%, and other major American stock indexes also jumped.

Supporters say Huang is the central person in the AI boom. They believe Nvidia, American technology and investor confidence all depend on him. Without Huang, they fear that the AI bubble may burst.

The writer thinks this argument is dangerous. Many AI companies have promised to spend huge amounts of money on chips. The government and business leaders therefore want the AI boom to continue. Huang's return also sends a message that important technology leaders may be treated as if they are above the law.

Many ordinary Americans and members of Congress are worried about national security and Nvidia's relationship with China. However, their concerns did not stop Huang's return. The article calls this an AI hostage economy: people are promised progress and economic safety, but are warned that regulation or accountability could make everything collapse.

20261124.background: 2026年11月中旬，美国在数日内连续发生微软服务中断、航空管制通信故障、银行系统异常和国家安全局内部通信受阻。密集事故引发了网络攻击和失控AI的猜测。文章并不把这些事件简单归因于敌对国家，而是从老旧基础设施、软件更新和AI加速漏洞修补的角度寻找共同原因。
20261124.overview:
文章先列举四起接连发生的美国数字系统故障，并说明官方解释为何难以获得公众信任。调查显示，空管事故与新路由器和基础设施升级有关；微软的大规模宕机则由一项运行数月后才暴露的软件补丁漏洞引发。银行和美国国家安全局的问题也都与软件更新有关。

这些事故之间未必存在直接联系，却可能共享一个更深层的背景：人工智能让企业能够以前所未有的速度发现安全漏洞，也迫使团队同时部署大量补丁。Anthropic的Mythos等模型提高了漏洞发现效率，但修补工作的数量与速度可能压垮老旧系统和人手不足的运维团队。短期内，这会带来更多故障和公众焦虑；长期看，大量漏洞被清除后，系统有望变得更安全。文章的核心判断是，防御网络攻击的加速行动本身，也会制造新的短期风险。
20261124.pet:
Several important computer systems in America failed within a few days. Microsoft services stopped working, air-traffic control had communication problems, several banks had technical trouble, and the National Security Agency lost part of its classified communication system. Many Americans wondered whether this was an enemy attack.

Officials gave different explanations. The air-traffic problem was linked to a faulty new router. Microsoft's outage came from a software patch with a hidden bug. The problems at some banks and the NSA were also connected to software updates. There is little evidence that hackers or uncontrolled AI caused the incidents.

However, AI may still be part of the story. AI tools can find weaknesses in computer systems much faster than people could before. This creates pressure on companies and government agencies to repair many problems at the same time.

Anthropic's Mythos model is very good at finding and using software weaknesses. Selected organisations use it to check their own code before criminals can attack it. This is useful, but the number and speed of repairs can overwhelm technical teams and old systems.

In the short term, Americans may see more outages and become more afraid of cyber-attacks. In the long term, the repairs should remove many weaknesses and make computer systems safer. The main idea is that efforts to improve security can create new risks while the work is being done.

20261123.background: AMD是全球主要芯片公司之一，由苏姿丰领导，并一直试图在人工智能加速器市场挑战英伟达。Hunterbrook Media与投资机构Hunterbrook Capital有关联：前者发布调查报道，后者可能通过做空相关股票获利。因此，阅读这类报告时既要核对其中提出的财务与合规问题，也要留意发布者自身的利益关系。
20261123.overview:
文章分为两条相互关联的线索。第一条线索是Hunterbrook对AMD的调查：报告质疑AMD数百亿美元的担保、基础设施安排和未来股权投资，并关注其中国合作方可能带来的出口合规风险。AMD股价因此下跌约7%，但报告并未证明AMD违法，而且发布报告的关联基金持有AMD空头仓位。华尔街分析师仍普遍看好AMD。

第二条线索是OpenAI降低对英伟达依赖的计划。OpenAI正在设计自有芯片、考虑购买Google TPU，并推进与AMD的六吉瓦算力合作。TensorWave将成为该合作的首家新云服务商，为OpenAI提供457兆瓦算力。文章由此说明，AMD既面临财务与合规质疑，也迎来了人工智能公司主动分散英伟达供应风险所带来的巨大机会。
20261123.pet:
AMD's share price fell about 7% after Hunterbrook Media published a critical report. The report questioned AMD's large financial promises and some of its relationships with Chinese companies. It also raised concerns about US export rules. However, the report did not prove that AMD broke the law. Hunterbrook Capital also has a short position in AMD, so it may make money if AMD's share price falls.

Wall Street analysts still believe AMD may grow in the long term. Most analysts rate the stock as a strong buy. This is partly because large AI companies want more choices instead of depending only on Nvidia.

OpenAI now uses Nvidia chips for almost all of its models, so problems at Nvidia could seriously affect it. Anthropic already uses chips from Google, AMD, Amazon and Nvidia. This gives Anthropic more flexibility and can lower its costs.

OpenAI is trying to build a similar system. It is designing its own chip, may buy Google TPUs and has signed a large agreement with AMD. The AMD deal could provide six gigawatts of computing capacity.

TensorWave will be the first new cloud company in this deal. It will provide 457 megawatts across several US data centres and may need three times as many workers. AMD therefore faces real risks, but it also has a major chance to benefit as AI companies reduce their dependence on Nvidia.
